pageCache.pageTitle: Horsington Church School - Christian Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Christian Vision and Values
Mission Statement
We are a community of learners and seek to create, within a Christian ethos, a happy, secure and stimulating learning environment in which all members of the school community can grow in self-esteem and develop their full potential.
Statement of Religious Ethos
Recognising its historic foundation, the school will preserve and develop its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the Church at parish and diocesan level.
The school aims to serve its community by providing an education of the highest quality within the context of Christian belief and practice. It encourages an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith, and promotes Christian values through the experience it offers to all its pupils.
Aims of the School
The school aims to help children to develop a Christian understanding of the world in which they live, and to respect other world views, religions and values.
This will enable them to:
Achieve their full academic potential
Develop lively and enquiring minds
Develop independence
Remain safe and secure whilst at school
listItems: Remain safe and secure whilst at school

pageCache.pageTitle: Horsington Church School - Church and Community
pageCache.text:
Church and Community
A Message from the Reverend Kevin Rogers
Greetings: At Horsington Church School we see all truth as God’s truth, and all people, no matter what their age as full human beings made in God’s image. We want our learners to grow in every aspect of their life and being – and so to grow in self-esteem and develop their full potential. We want them to have that balance of independence, and yet recognise the strength of community. So for us it is important that we are a community of learners. All people, young and old, perform best and grow best is an environment that is caring, secure and stimulating – allowing curiosity, and giving the skills to exercise it. God has given us the ability to dream dreams – and we want our learners to dream great dreams, and achieve great things.
St. Johns Church
Statement of Religious Ethos
Recognising its historic foundation, the school will preserve and develop its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the Church at parish and diocesan level.
The school aims to serve its community by providing an education of the highest quality within the context of Christian belief and practice. It encourages an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith, and promotes Christian values through the experience it offers to all its pupils.
Our Village
As a village school we have strong links with the community we serve. Although many of our pupils come from outside the villages of Horsington and South Cheriton, we play an active part in village events. Members of the community come into school to talk to the children and we take our children into the village for local and environmental studies.
Villager – a Horsington & South Cheriton monthly publication
February 2026 edition
November 2025 edition
To view past and present copies of the Villager go to Wincanton Window and click on the ‘Villages’ link.

Our Values
Our Christian values of Kindness, Love, Perseverance, Forgiveness, Trust and Respect are central to everything we do at Horsington Church School. We believe the fostering and maintaining of caring and nurturing relationships, and a happy and safe environment, ensures our children are spirituality, socially and emotionally supported.
At Horsington, we have a purposeful, safe, and stimulating environment where everyone is encouraged and supported to ‘Be the best version of themselves.’ Everyone will work together, to ensure our learners, staff and parents benefit from a culture which promotes self-esteem, trust, compassion, mutual respect, and inclusivity. Everyone within the school community can reach their full potential and may enjoy ‘Life in all its fullness.’
We have high expectations of our children, encouraging them to be polite, well mannered, and helpful to one other, to become lifelong learners and good citizens.
It is important that the children understand what acceptable behaviour is, equally unacceptable behaviour and the consequences of such behaviour. We want to ensure that the children at Horsington have the skills, strategies, and vocabulary to equip them for life now and in the future.

Christian Distinctiveness

Collective Worship
Each day we hold a Christian Act of Worship. This is an important part of our day. As we are a Church School our Acts of Worship are sympathetic with the views and traditions of the Church. We try to make each day’s collective worship slightly different and children can expect to sing, listen to stories, listen to musicians, watch short plays, and make points themselves. All teachers as well as our local clergy take our Acts of Worship.
Each Friday we hold a Celebration Assembly where we celebrate the children's efforts and learning - through our merits and class sashes.
Under the provisions of the Education Reform Act 1988 any parent wishing to withdraw a child from collective worship should make a written request to the Head teacher.
Please read our Collective Worship Policy
Our Collective Worship links our School Values – Perseverance, Kindness, Forgiveness, Trust, Respect, Love. The chosen themes are changed on a termly basis and work in a two year rolling programme:
Year A: Generosity, Compassion, Courage, Forgiveness, Friendship, Respect.
Year B: Thankfulness, Trust, Perseverance, Justice, Service, Truthfulness.

pageCache.pageTitle: Horsington Church School - Head's Welcome and Vision
pageCache.text:
Head's Welcome
A warm welcome from Mrs Barge
"That they may have life, life in all its fullness” John 10
Horsington Church School ensures that every child can flourish, a place where we value every child as an individual and develop children academically, socially, emotionally, and spiritually within a happy and nurturing environment. Together we give our children a place to develop their faith, make lasting friendships, engage in high quality learning, and most importantly have fun and laugh!
As Early starters at Horsington, our children ‘Explore, Play, and Learn’ in a safe, stimulating, and flourishing environment, developing essential learning characteristics and relationships, thus setting a strong foundation for their educational journey. We strive for all our children to engage in a relevant and opportunistic curriculum, whilst utilising the outdoor learning and community environment.
By providing an excellent education grounded in a distinctively Christian ethos, we strive to promote the values of our Christian faith throughout daily life and take pride in our Christian ethos. Our strong partnerships with the church and local community enhance children’s knowledge and understanding of our faith.
It is our school Christian values of Love, Respect, Forgiveness, Kindness, Trust and Perseverance that we hope our children will take with them into their future lives.

Wraparound Care
We understand the need for childcare outside of normal school hours and offer a breakfast club during termtime. This operates from 08.00-08.45 Monday to Friday and is available for all Horsington pupils from reception to year 6. Breakfast is provided for children and also a range of activities while they attend.
We also offer an after school care club during termtime. This operates between 3.30-5.00pm Monday to Thursday. The children can enjoy a range of activities - games, arts and crafts, reading and outdoor play. A drink and healthy snack will be provided.
All sessions need to be booked and paid for in advance using the parent portal.

pageCache.text:
Home Learning – Calculations
Parents often ask for advice about how to support their children with calculations. Our Calculation Policy for Mathematics sets out how we teach the children to calculate, and is written in order to help you support your child more effectively.
In addition, the videos below demonstrate how we teach calculations in school. Many thanks to Moortown Primary School for making these videos.
Maths Leaflet for parents – your home is also an amazing maths resource

Home Learning
The role of parents in promoting positive attitudes to their child’s learning is never underestimated and all of our children are encouraged to undertake a wide range of activities to support their schoolwork.
From entry to school reading books should be taken home each day for reading practice. This is the first and most important form of homework. Throughout the Primary years the importance of time and space to read and listen to adults read is paramount.
As the child progresses through the school he/she will experience other forms of homework:
Children need support to complete their homework with care. Should your child experience anxiety about a task please let the class teacher know and we will do all we can to help.
A Homework Booklet is available to parents outlining ways you can support your child’s homework. You may also find this BBC website useful.
